name: Tish Gervais
context: The name Brian lived under in the 70s and 80s - Natalia first, then Tish Gervais, Miss Thing all the way through, as James puts it. James says Tish's pronouns are she and her; Brian's friend Tony Zanetta later called Tish a vessel who kept Brian alive

name: New York
context: Brian arrived in 1974, just after Stonewall, to transition - he says he couldn't wait to get out of Rhode Island, and found his mentors in the nightclubs

name: The Gilded Grape
heard: the G.G., the Gilded Grape / Gildegrave / Gilded Gate
context: The club for trans women and drag queens on Eighth Avenue and 45th Street, under the Camelot building, that James is obsessed with. Brian lived there in those years: a free buffet if you bought a drink, a DJ, lip-sync shows, pageants and plenty of drama, he says - and he learned everything from the women there. Later it moved up the street to the old Peppermint Lounge

name: Federico Fellini
context: Brian's idol - he says all Fellini's films had people like them in them. At the after-party Dinah Prince brought Tish over; Brian says Fellini looked her up and down and said come to Rome

name: Trans Figured: My Journey from Boy to Woman to Man
heard: your book / the book is Transfigured
context: Brian's memoir. It opens on the night of the Fellini premiere and ends with a list of fifty trans women from those years who were his mentors

name: Brian Belovitch
context: Guest. Writer, actor and counsellor who came to New York from Rhode Island in 1974, lived as Natalia and then Tish Gervais through the 70s and 80s and went back to living as Brian from 1987; he calls himself a gender outlier and tells it all in his memoir Trans Figured

name: Rhode Island
context: Where Brian grew up and did his first drag with the RISD kids; he says it was Republican and homophobic then and he couldn't wait to leave - and he went back to it more than once to start again

name: Gabriel Rotello
context: Says hello through Brian, who was seeing him that Saturday. Brian says Gabriel was one of the people who helped him in the 80s; they met at Nelson Sullivan's, and Gabriel put Tish in his Downtown Dukes and Divas shows - rehearsing with real musicians in his loft on Tenth Avenue

name: Nelson Sullivan
context: Taped a little cabaret show of Tish's and raved about her to Gabriel - Brian met Gabriel at Nelson's on New Year's or Christmas Eve; Nelson also filmed Tish's Dukes and Divas spot

name: Antonio Lopez
context: The great fashion illustrator. He spotted Tish dancing at Hurrah - who is that mad woman, I must meet her - gave her his card, drew her in his studio and sent her to Studio 54 to be one of the girls for opening night; Brian modelled for him again in the 80s

name: The 220 Club
context: After-hours club where Brian worked after the Gilded Grape - mostly trans, a little stage for lip-sync shows; he tended bar there and says when the police knocked he jumped the bar and ran into the freezer with the cash box

name: Carmen D'Alessio
context: Brian knocked on Studio 54's door in the middle of the afternoon, sat down in the building site and kept asking for Carmen until she came - and told him the swing girls were already cast

name: Randy Barbato
context: Co-host; says he had no idea what Tish was going through back then - he and Fenton were home in bed by half past eleven

name: United States Army
context: Brian's husband enlisted; Tish followed as an army wife - 'how am I going to fit in that scene?'

context: The 1986 premiere of Ginger and Fred at MoMA, a pink carpet up Fifth Avenue and the after-party at Trump Tower. James calls it a social triumph for Tish; in the group photo Brian says someone shoved Tish to the ground, so she vogued on the floor - the picture ran everywhere

context: Tish dolled up as the ultimate glamorous sex pot - La Dolce Vita and Juliet of the Spirits rolled into one - walking the pink carpet up Fifth Avenue among the downtown crowd in plunging necklines, until a spaghetti strap gave way in the photo
